rewrites.summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score, and a trans traveler here stands under that national framework as it operates countrywide. Consensual same-sex activity is not criminalised, but the 2023 laws ban same-sex marriage and legal gender recognition and effectively ban trans-specific healthcare, so marriage-based partner status and corrected identity documents are unavailable. The national court system designated the international LGBT+ movement an 'extremist' organisation in November 2023, and enforcement followed: 101 'extremism'-related convictions with sentences up to 12 years, 81 people found guilty in 98 administrative cases since January 2024, and at least 139 individuals affected by anti-LGBT+ law enforcement between 2022 and 2024, with 'gay propaganda' penalties for individuals up to 400,000 rubles (about £3,600) or 15 days' detention.

blindSourceSummaries: National framework note (June 2025): consensual same-sex activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and legal gender recognition are banned and trans-specific healthcare is effectively banned; the national court system designated the international LGBT+ movement an 'extremist' organisation in November 2023; 2022-2024 enforcement affected at least 139 individuals, with individual penalties up to 400,000 rubles (about £3,600) or 15 days' detention. The note records no division-specific information.

Monitoring report (June 2025): courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions for participation in the international movement or displaying its symbols, with sentences up to 12 years; 81 people were found guilty in 98 administrative cases since January 2024, mostly for displaying banned symbols online. No division-specific detail.
